page.title: Building real-time applications with React and WebSockets
page.description: How to structure React apps around live data, persistent connections, and real-time user interactions.

text.content: Real-time features can make an app feel alive.

rich_text.plain_text: Real-time features can make an app feel alive.

text.content: Chat messages appear without refreshing. Notifications show up the second something happens. Dashboards update while you watch them. Collaborative tools stop feeling like everyone is emailing a spreadsheet around like it is 2007.

rich_text.plain_text: Chat messages appear without refreshing. Notifications show up the second something happens. Dashboards update while you watch them. Collaborative tools stop feeling like everyone is emailing a spreadsheet around like it is 2007.

text.content: That is the fun part.

rich_text.plain_text: That is the fun part.

text.content: The less fun part is that real-time systems come with a few new problems: dropped connections, duplicate events, reconnects, stale state, scaling issues, and users who close their laptop halfway through an action and then blame you.

rich_text.plain_text: The less fun part is that real-time systems come with a few new problems: dropped connections, duplicate events, reconnects, stale state, scaling issues, and users who close their laptop halfway through an action and then blame you.

text.content: For React apps, Socket.IO is a great way to get started. It gives you real-time, event-based communication between your client and server, plus helpful features like reconnection, rooms, and fallback transports.

text.content: Let’s walk through how it works, how to wire it into React, and what to watch out for before calling it production-ready.

text.content: Final Thoughts

rich_text.plain_text: Final Thoughts

text.content: Real-time features are fun because they make your app feel alive.

rich_text.plain_text: Real-time features are fun because they make your app feel alive.

text.content: They are also a little trickier than normal request-response code. Connections drop. Events arrive twice. Users reconnect. State gets stale. Servers restart. Somewhere, someone closes their laptop at the exact wrong moment.

text.content: Socket.IO gives you a friendly way to handle a lot of that complexity, especially for chat, notifications, dashboards, and collaborative features.
